input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: Changing `fg is not None` to a truthiness check `if fg:` skips color index 0 (integer 0), which is valid (black in 256-color palette). The same applies to `bg` at line 684.
- rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=0)` or `bg=0`. The falsy value is skipped, so no escape code is emitted and the text is rendered in the default color with no error. This is silent wrong output. It also silently ignores an empty tuple/list or empty string instead of raising an error.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: the truthiness check on fg/bg replaces `is not None`, so index 0 is skipped. It gives the same failure path, `style('x', fg=0)` or `bg=0` rendering in the default color with no error.
